(a) Information Provided to the Prisoner Update Processing System (PUPS).—
        (1) Section 202(x)(3)(b)(i)(i).—Section 202(x)(3)(B)(i)(I) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 402(x)(3)(B)(i)(I)) is amended by—
            (A) inserting “first, middle, and last” before “names”; 
            (B) striking the comma after the words “social security account numbers” and inserting “or taxpayer identification numbers, prison assigned inmate numbers, last known addresses,”; 
            (C) inserting “dates of release or anticipated dates of release, dates of work release,” before “and, to the extent available”; and 
            (D) by inserting “and clause (iv) of this subparagraph” after “paragraph (1)”.  
        (2) Section 1611(e)(1)(i)(i)(i).—Section 1611(e)(1)(I)(i)(I) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1382(e)(1)(I)(i)(I)) is amended by—
            (A) inserting “first, middle, and last” before “names”; 
            (B) striking the comma after the words “social security account numbers” and inserting “or taxpayer identification numbers, prison assigned inmate numbers, last known addresses,”; 
            (C) inserting “dates of release or anticipated dates of release, dates of work release,” before “and, to the extent available”; and 
            (D) by inserting “and clause (iv) of this subparagraph” after “this paragraph”.   
    (b) Authority of Secretary of the Treasury to Access PUPS.—
        (1) Section 202(x)(3)(b).—Section 202(x)(3)(B) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 402(x)(3)(B)) is amended—
            (A) in clause (iv), by inserting before the period the following: “, for statistical and research activities conducted by Federal and State agencies, and to the Secretary of the Treasury for the purposes of tax administration, debt collection, and identifying, preventing, and recovering improper payments under federally funded programs”; and 
            (B) by adding at the end the following:“(v)(I) The Commissioner may disclose information received pursuant to this paragraph to any officer, employee, agent, or contractor of the Department of the Treasury whose official duties require such information to assist in the identification, prevention, and recovery of improper payments or in the collection of delinquent debts owed to the United States, including payments certified by the head of an executive, judicial, or legislative paying agency, and payments made to individuals whose eligibility, or continuing eligibility, to participate in a Federal program (including those administered by a State or political subdivision thereof) is being reviewed.“(II) Notwithstanding the provisions of section 552a of title 5, United States Code, or any other provision of Federal or State law, the Secretary of the Treasury may compare information disclosed under subclause (I) with any other personally identifiable information derived from a Federal system of records or similar records maintained by a Federal contractor, a Federal grantee, or an entity administering a Federal program or activity, and may redisclose such comparison of information to any paying or administering agency and to the head of the Federal Bureau of Prisons and the head of any State agency charged with the administration of prisons with respect to inmates whom the Secretary of the Treasury has determined may have been issued, or facilitated in the issuance of, an improper payment.“(III) The comparison of information disclosed under subclause (I) shall not be considered a matching program for purposes of section 552a of title 5, United States Code.”.  
        (2) Section 1611(e)(1)(i).—Section 1611(e)(1)(I) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1382(e)(1)(I)) is amended—
            (A) in clause (iii), by inserting before the period the following: “, for statistical and research activities conducted by Federal and State agencies, and to the Secretary of the Treasury for the purposes of tax administration, debt collection, and identifying, preventing, and recovering improper payments under federally funded programs”; and 
            (B) by adding at the end the following:“(v)(I) The Commissioner may disclose information received pursuant to this paragraph to any officer, employee, agent, or contractor of the Department of the Treasury whose official duties require such information to assist in the identification, prevention, and recovery of improper payments or in the collection of delinquent 
debts owed to the United States, including payments certified by the head of an executive, judicial, or legislative paying agency, and payments made to individuals whose eligibility, or continuing eligibility, to participate in a Federal program (including those administered by a State or political subdivision thereof) is being reviewed.“(II) Notwithstanding the provisions of section 552a of title 5, United States Code, or any other provision of Federal or State law, the Secretary of the Treasury may compare information disclosed under subclause (I) with any other personally identifiable information derived from a Federal system of records or similar records maintained by a Federal contractor, a Federal grantee, or an entity administering a Federal program or activity and may redisclose such comparison of information to any paying or administering agency and to the head of the Federal Bureau of Prisons and the head of any State agency charged with the administration of prisons with respect to inmates whom the Secretary of the Treasury has determined may have been issued, or facilitated in the issuance of, an improper payment.“(III) The comparison of information disclosed under subclause (I) shall not be considered a matching program for purposes of section 552a of title 5, United States Code.”.   
    (c) Conforming Amendment to the Do Not Pay Initiative.—Section 5(a)(2) of the Improper Payments Elimination and Recovery Improvement Act of 2012 (31 U.S.C. 3321 note) is amended by adding at the end the following:“(F) Information regarding incarcerated individuals maintained by the Commissioner of Social Security under sections 202(x) and 1611(e) of the Social Security Act.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that references to State agencies and contractors bring outside parties into a federal process. But the section only expands the prisoner data reported to the Social Security Administration and authorizes disclosure, comparison and redisclosure of that data among the Commissioner, Treasury and prison agencies to curb improper payments. Sharing information with a State prison agency is not consulting it before a federal decision. The section creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: may redisclose such comparison of information to any paying or administering agency and to the head of the Federal Bureau of Prisons and the head of any State agency charged with the administration of prisons

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury to access and share data with other government agencies (including state prison agencies) for the purpose of debt collection and preventing improper payments. It does not require the government to consult with, coordinate with, or seek input from outside parties before making a decision. The interaction described is one-way data sharing for administrative enforcement, not participatory decision-making. While state agencies are mentioned as recipients of information, they are not involved in the decision-making process itself.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary of the Treasury may compare information disclosed under subclause (I) with any other personally identifiable information derived from a Federal system of records or similar records maintained by a Federal contractor, a Federal grantee, or an entity administering a Federal program or activity and may redisclose such comparison of information to any paying or administering agency and to the head of the Federal Bureau of Prisons and the head of any State agency charged with the administration of prisons

opus.w: The section changes what prisoner data goes into PUPS and lets the Social Security Administration and Treasury share and compare that data to find improper payments. State prison agencies and contractors appear only as recipients or holders of data, not as parties consulted before a federal decision. The tempting reading treats data sharing with state agencies as coordination. But nobody outside the federal government gives input or can challenge the decision, so there is no participation.
opus.s: may redisclose such comparison of information to any paying or administering agency and to the head of the Federal Bureau of Prisons and the head of any State agency charged with the administration of prisons with respect to inmates whom the Secretary of the Treasury has determined may have been issued, or facilitated in the issuance of, an improper payment.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** The section names outside parties: "contractor[s] of the Department of the Treasury," "a Federal grantee," and "the head of any State agency charged with the administration of prisons." It also mentions "State agencies" doing statistical research. That could look like coordination with outsiders.
2. **Why it fails:** These are one-way flows of information. The Commissioner may hand data to Treasury, and Treasury may pass match results on to paying agencies and prison officials. No outside party is asked for input before a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue. Sharing information is not participation.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the sharing of data between federal agencies and with state prison administrators for the purpose of identifying improper payments. It does not require the federal government to consult with or coordinate with outside parties before making a decision. The state agencies are recipients of information, not participants in a decision-making process such as an advisory board or public hearing. The interaction is administrative and unilateral from the perspective of the federal decision-maker.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of the Treasury may compare information disclosed under subclause (I) with any other personally identifiable information derived from a Federal system of records or similar records maintained by a Federal contractor, a Federal grantee, or an entity administering a Federal program or activity and may redisclose such comparison of information to any paying or administering agency and to the head of the Federal Bureau of Prisons and the head of any State agency charged with the administration of prisons
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Secretary of the Treasury can share information with "the head of any State agency charged with the administration of prisons," this constitutes coordination or consultation with outside entities (states). However, the text describes a one-way disclosure of data for administrative purposes (debt collection/improper payment recovery), not a two-way consultation or coordination process where the state provides input into a federal decision. The state is a recipient of information, not a participant in the decision-making process. Furthermore, the primary actors are federal agencies (Social Security, Treasury) and federal contractors/grantees. The sharing of data with state prison heads is an administrative enforcement mechanism, not a participatory process like a hearing, advisory committee, or required consultation before a decision.
